text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the July 29 edition of some Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Military reform is necessary to maintain production of modern weapons and military hardware.
- Russia's Finance Ministry is to present the 1998 draft budget to the State Duma lower house of parliament on August 1, says First Deputy Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin.
- Good crops expected in Russia this year may present a lot of harvesting problems because of lack of financing and shortage of agricultural machinery.
- Insufficient and irregular funding holds up fuel deliveries to Russia's North.
- The government has prepared a programme of reforming enterprises which would open a new stage of economic reforms in Russia, says a senior Finance Ministry official.
- According to President Boris Yeltsin's decree, a 0,5 percent tax is introduced on foreign currency buyings as of July 29. The decree is published by the paper.
- The state budget loses $100 million quarterly because of bootleg vodka smuggled from the republic of Nothern Ossetia in Russia's Caucasus.

- A new land code prepared by parliament "not only flagrantly violates constitutional rights of citizens and legal entities but also ignores interests of the state", says the President's letter addressed to the heads of parliamentary chambers.
- President's outstanding activity during his holiday demonstrates he is on the rise both physically and emotionally, says the president administration's paper.
- President Yeltsin's rating now is as low as it was in January and February 1996, says a public opinion expert.
- The opposition paper doubts results of the governor's election in Irkutsk region.
